key_insight: K-Bench introduces a clinician-calibrated benchmark for testing how well large language models handle high-risk, multi-turn mental health conversations. It helps reveal whether models stay safe and appropriate across evolving scenarios such as suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, and substance misuse.
problem_solved: Current LLM evaluations often miss how models behave in realistic, shifting mental health conversations, especially in high-risk settings. This paper addresses the lack of a standardized, clinically grounded benchmark for measuring safety and quality in these sensitive interactions.
method: Built K-Bench using 200 multi-turn vignettes covering suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, and no-risk cases.
Clinician-calibrated the benchmark to reflect realistic and medically relevant risk scenarios.
Evaluated 125 model configurations across 33 base models from 14 providers to compare safety behavior at scale.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a rigorous way to test and compare model safety in one of the most sensitive real-world use cases. It can guide model selection, red-teaming, and safer deployment of LLMs in mental health support applications.
visual_elements: A flow diagram showing the benchmark pipeline: vignette design → clinician calibration → model evaluation → safety scoring
A comparison bar chart of model performance across risk categories
An icon-based dashboard for the five vignette types: suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, no-risk
A heatmap showing safety/appropriateness across multi-turn conversation stages
paper_title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
paper_authors: Laura M. Vowels, Matthew J. Vowels, Shivali Sharma, Apoorv Jha, Rehnuma Choudhury
